variants.answer: I’d treat the save as an unknown outcome rather than assume it failed. I’d keep the coordinator’s edits on screen, mark the update “Checking status…” and retry the status check using the same request ID so we don’t create duplicates. If the server confirms the save, I’d show when it was saved; if it confirms it wasn’t, I’d offer a clear “Retry save” action without asking them to re-enter anything. If status remains unavailable, I’d say the outcome is still uncertain, preserve the draft locally, and explain what to do next. I’d also log these cases and track duplicate updates, lost edits, and time to resolution. In testing, I’d simulate disconnects before and after server commit and verify that recovery neither loses edits nor creates a second task update.

variants.answer: I’d avoid showing a generic failure message because the update may already have reached the server. I’d preserve the user’s changes, show that we’re checking whether the save completed, and then either confirm success or offer a retry. I’d use an idempotency key to prevent duplicate updates and test interruptions at different points in the save flow.
